name_en: Dayi Jin Zhen Bai Lian (Golden Needle White Lotus)
name_ru: Да И Цзинь Чжэнь Бай Лянь
processing: Ripe pu-erh from high-grade, tender Yunnan large-leaf sun-dried tea, wet-piled and pressed; the fine buds set it apart from coarser-leaf ripe blends.
harvest_season: Not sold by picking: tender buds are selected for the blend, and the batch number and pressing date identify each production.
appearance_dry: A cake of tight, needle-thin buds with visible golden tips, chestnut in colour with a greyish cast.
appearance_wet: Small, soft, fine reddish-brown buds and young leaves.
taste_profile: Smooth and clean with very little off-flavour, marked by a lotus-leaf aroma that is its signature; honeyed notes are said to grow with age.

brewing.notes: Fine buds give up flavour fast, so keep the early steeps short. A long steep makes it heavy and hides the lotus aroma.

vintage_note: Sold by batch and pressing date as a 357 g cake. Pressing and retail do not always line up: batch 2501 was pressed on 26 June 2025 and reached shops only in autumn 2026, so read the date on the wrapper. Younger cakes lean to lotus, while older ones are described as leaning to aged notes.
description:
Jin Zhen Bai Lian is Dayi's fine-bud ripe cake and a rare ripe tea known mainly for one aroma: lotus leaf, not the wood, date or aged notes most people expect. The first sip often surprises people for that reason.

The name describes the tea. The 'golden needles' are tight, thin buds with visible golden tips, and the 'white lotus' refers to the greyish chestnut colour and the lotus scent. It starts from high-grade, tender Yunnan large-leaf material, fermented and pressed.

The cup is smooth and clean, with a bright red liquor and almost no pile funk. Fine buds extract quickly, so a heavy hand makes it dull. Use short steeps and water slightly below the boil if the first cup seems thick.

Buyers ask whether the lotus scent is added; that question comes up regularly in Chinese tea discussion, and it is worth tasting critically. It is also a popular gift, with a market price that moves around, so compare batch and date as well as price.
history:
The tea dates to 2005. Promotional accounts from around the brand say it won a gold medal at an international tea expo in October 2005, though they name the event inconsistently, sometimes as a Beijing expo and sometimes as a China expo.

It has since been repressed in batches, and the 2501 batch was marketed as a return to the 2005 style.
